subject: Appendix: External provider ownership & dataflow — FinCo RFI
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@finco.com>, procurement@finco.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Appendix: External provider ownership & dataflow — FinCo RFI

Hi Sam / FinCo procurement team,

Thanks again for the RFI opportunity. Per your request in section 3.2, attached is a concise appendix that maps every external provider we rely on for the Redwood hosted inference stack, the ownership model (vendor vs. sub‑contractor vs. affiliate), and a high‑level dataflow note for each provider. The goal is to give you the minimum evidence you need to satisfy your vendor‑risk team without exchanging our entire vendor playbook.

What you will find attached: 
- third-party-ownership-and-dataflow.csv — CSV rows: provider, purpose, ownership, region(s), data classification, access controls, SOC2 / ISO attestation status
- cloud-affiliate-change-notice.pdf — brief notice documenting a small infrastructure change related to an EU edge caching partner (dates and mitigations included)
- eu-key-usage-diagram.png — simplified diagram showing where customer-encrypted keys are used for EU workloads
- dpa-link.txt — link to our standard DPA and the FinCo‑specific addendum we proposed last month

A few clarifications up front so your security reviewers see the context: 
- Primary compute: we host customer inference on dedicated pools (Redwood Dedicated) or our hosted multi‑tenant API; the CSV marks whether an external provider is in the control plane, data plane, or both.
- Key management: for EU‑resident workloads we offer customer‑managed keys via KMS; the diagram shows where KMS keys are used and where we never persist plaintext.
- Temporary vendor change: the PDF explains an imminent shift of a small EU edge cache operator to a partner called NimbleEdge; this affects only cached model artifacts (read‑only) and does not touch KV cache or token-level logs.

If you want, we can:
- produce a one‑page A3 that maps your required controls to each vendor line item; or
- schedule a 30‑minute call with Ben (security / vendor ops) to walk through the EU change notice and key handling.

Next steps: please confirm which controls your vendor team wants evidence for (e.g., SOC2 report, contract clause, penetration testing evidence) and we will prioritize.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0182

Attachment stubs: third-party-ownership-and-dataflow.csv (CSV), cloud-affiliate-change-notice.pdf (PDF), eu-key-usage-diagram.png (PNG), dpa-link.txt (TXT)
From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@finco.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, procurement@finco.com
Cc: security@finco.com
Date: Mon, 1 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Appendix: External provider ownership & dataflow — FinCo RFI

Naomi, thank you for the quick turnaround and the attachments — I can confirm receipt. A couple of questions from our vendor risk squad after an initial pass: 

1) The CSV lists NimbleEdge as an "affiliate" in eu-west-1 for artifact caching. Can you clarify contractual relationships: is there a sub‑processor agreement or an affiliate memorandum of understanding in place? We need the legal basis for their access.

2) The key usage diagram looks clear, but can you explicitly state whether we (FinCo) can enforce a customer‑managed KMS key such that no Redwood personnel can decrypt any customer tokens or logs for EU workloads? Our security team is strict on key separation and access logs.

3) For the cloud provider list: please indicate whether any providers have cross‑border replication enabled by default for backups. That is a blocker for our EU residency requirement.

Also please attach any SOC2 Type II artifact or ISO attestation you can share under an NDA. We can provide an NDA link if that makes it easier.

If you prefer, Ben's walkthrough would help — we typically book these as a separate vendor evidence call.

Sam Lee
Director, Vendor Risk
FinCo Bank
sam.lee@finco.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@finco.com>, procurement@finco.com
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2028 09:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Appendix: External provider ownership & dataflow — FinCo RFI

Sam — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers inline below and I attached two items you asked for under NDA: a redacted SOC2 Type II cover page (we can share the full report after an executed NDA) and a short contract exhibit template showing subprocessor terms.

1) NimbleEdge relationship: NimbleEdge is a contracted partner (not an equity affiliate). We maintain a standard subprocessor addendum with them; the PDF (cloud-affiliate-change-notice.pdf) includes the contract clause references and the transition timeline. Access is limited: read‑only for model artifact caches, no access to runtime KV caches or customer logs. Legal team confirmed the subprocessor addendum is in effect as of Apr 15, 2028.

2) Customer KMS enforcement: yes — for EU workloads you can opt into customer‑managed keys (CMK) in your preferred KMS. When CMK is enabled, Redwood never stores plaintext keys and we treat cryptographic operations as server‑side KMS calls that are auditable in your KMS logs. We will provide sample IAM guidance for key policies and CloudTrail/CIS logging references in the follow‑up.

3) Cross‑border replication: default backup replication is disabled for EU‑pinned accounts. The CSV has a "replication_default" column; for any provider listed with a "yes" we added a short note on how to disable it at account level. For clarity: snapshots for model artifacts are stored in eu‑regions only when a customer elects EU pinning.

Attachments included in this message (stubs): soc2-redacted-cover.pdf, subprocessor-exhibit-template.docx. Also included: a short checklist we use for vendor‑risk calls.

If helpful, Marissa can run a 45‑minute technical walkthrough (network diagrams, KMS policy examples, and proof points) next week — Marissa?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Manager, Vendor Ops
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachment stubs: soc2-redacted-cover.pdf (PDF), subprocessor-exhibit-template.docx (DOCX), vendor-evidence-checklist.pdf (PDF)

Ben / Naomi — this is great, thanks. We see the high‑level answers we need for the preliminary RFI. Next steps from our side:

- Procurement will route the NDA this afternoon (we prefer to use our template).
- Security will take the 45‑minute walkthrough — proposed slot: Thu 10:00 AM CET (please confirm availability).

Appreciate the quick responses — I will confirm the call time after procurement shares the NDA link.

Sam

FinCo Bank
